purpose: Performance thresholds DEFINED BEFORE results are interpreted (issue #74 §3).
note: These are acceptance lines for the device harnesses. A number is read against the line its scenario names; the Leaflet-ceiling crossing uses interaction_to_paint_ms.p95 and pan_frame_ms.p95.

first_contentful_paint_ms.rationale: Web Vitals 'good' FCP is <=1.8 s; >3 s on a mid-range device/4G reads as a slow page. The app is a static site, so FCP is dominated by HTML+CSS+vendored Leaflet, not data.

time_to_interactive_map_ms.rationale: Time from navigation until the map accepts a Lens drag. >5 s means the user waits on data fetch+parse before the core interaction works; the partitioning finding targets this.

interaction_to_paint_ms.rationale: During a continuous Lens drag each recompute+repaint must land fast enough that the lens feels attached to the pointer. Nielsen's 0.1 s is the 'instantaneous' bound; beyond ~150 ms p95 the lens visibly lags the cursor. This is the PRIMARY ceiling metric.

pan_frame_ms.rationale: Panning is continuous animation. 16.7 ms = 60 fps (smooth); 33.3 ms = 30 fps (the floor below which touch panning reads as stutter, most visible on iPad). p95 is used so occasional long frames count.

js_heap_mb.rationale: No hard pass/fail (performance.memory is Chromium-only and coarse). Flagged above ~500 MB JS heap as a tablet-stability risk worth noting, not a gate.

ceiling_definition.metric: the synthetic feature count at which interaction_to_paint_ms.p95 first exceeds acceptable_p95 (150 ms) during a Lens drag, OR pan_frame_ms.p95 first exceeds 33.3 ms during a pan, on a real device
